reviewer_scopes.E: tests, CI, platform claims, and maintainability

findings.summary: Duplicate keys and non-finite values in scanner or policy JSON could be consumed permissively.
Deep repository YAML could escape the documented exit contract through parser recursion.
Lazy block-quote continuations and indented examples could be misclassified as authoritative skill prose.
The root CLI truncated machine JSON and remapped lifecycle exit 4.
Extension failures could be wrapped in a success-status envelope.
Finding-group and priority documents were not fully cross-checked against source findings.
Secret-bearing authenticated workflows allowed branch-selected manual dispatch.
Published profile artifact and coverage-state inventories differed from workflow behavior.
Several published examples, flags, and implementation-status statements were stale or not executable as documented.
Provenance emitted four subjects while its public schema and documentation required three.
The review incorrectly changed the release contract to CycloneDX 1.6 while pinned Syft 1.49.0 emits CycloneDX 1.7.
Representative migration and adoption-example records were validated as metadata rather than executed end to end.
Release readiness could reuse stale test totals without fresh exact-source validation evidence.
The committed readiness record was stale and did not clearly identify itself as a historical reviewed-main snapshot.
The API-fuzzing integration workflow was absent from workflow inventory regression coverage.

fixes: Added bounded strict JSON parsing to scanner, policy, SBOM, and static repository configuration boundaries.
Added event-level YAML depth, document, and node bounds with fail-closed exit 3 behavior.
Expanded non-authoritative skill segmentation and fingerprint classification.
Preserved complete machine output and exact scanner versus lifecycle exit categories.
Cross-validated extension status, finding groups, priorities, profile artifacts, and coverage states.
Made secret-bearing authenticated workflows schedule-only and enforced that contract in initialization and doctor checks.
Aligned provenance, SBOM, release-readiness, migration, example, CLI, and generated documentation contracts.
Added exact-source release validation evidence and executable preservation tests for all eleven migrations and examples.
accepted_limitations: A completed scanner run is not proof that an application is secure.
Complete native Minimal and Standard scanning is validated on Linux x86_64; other advertised platforms remain conditional or experimental as cataloged.
Live Docker targets and GitHub OIDC signing require controlled GitHub-hosted environments.
Installed extension code and external agent behavior remain maintainer trust decisions.
deferred_items: Add explicit download-byte ceilings and fully streaming archive-member limits as defense-in-depth availability hardening.
Complete profile container runners, native Windows execution, and broader dynamic/runtime security remain post-v1 work.
A complete CommonMark semantic model beyond the explicitly classified authoritative structures remains deferred.
false_positives: A suspected duplicate workflow timeout was caused by overlapping review output; strict YAML parsing confirmed one timeout per job.
Duplicate archive members were initially described too broadly; implementation rejects conflicting executable targets while the manifest rejects ambiguous bundled paths.
platform_limits: Docker was unavailable, so live Checkov, ZAP, Schemathesis, and container-target checks were not claimed locally.
ShellCheck was unavailable; bash syntax validation and actionlint workflow linting passed independently.
Pinned Linux scanner installers intentionally reject this host; controlled scanner fixtures and the latest reviewed-main GitHub run provide the nearest safe evidence.
local_checks: all required CI job-equivalent test matrices
deterministic bundle generation and byte comparison
bundle, installation, doctor, and upgrade verification
release-candidate structure, checksums, SBOM, provenance, manifest, and readiness validation
agent, extension, migration, example, link, anchor, and generated-document validation
actionlint and JSON, YAML, TOML, Python, shell, skill, and Opengrep static validation
